name: Salesforce, Inc.
monetization: Sells AI agents (Agentforce) and data infrastructure (Data 360/Informatica) as paid add-ons to the world's largest CRM installed base; buys model capability from Anthropic and others rather than training its own.
description_md: Salesforce is the largest enterprise CRM vendor, monetizing AI through Agentforce — its platform for deploying autonomous agents across service, sales, and marketing — layered on the Data Cloud/Data 360 data layer, which the $8B Informatica acquisition substantially deepened. It is the bellwether test of whether incumbent SaaS can convert AI from a feature into net-new paid revenue: Agentforce ARR crossed $1B in the quarter ended April 2026, reaching $1.2B (+205% y/y), roughly eighteen months after launch.
ai_monetization_md: Three paid layers: (1) Agentforce ARR of $1.2B (April 2026), up from $500M in December 2025, sold via consumption ('flex credits') and per-conversation pricing on top of seat licenses; (2) Data 360 — combined Agentforce + Data 360 ARR reached $3.4B (+>200% y/y) including $1.1B of Informatica Cloud ARR; (3) the underlying subscription base, where Q1 FY2027 revenue was $11.1B (+~9-10% y/y) with subscription & support of $10.6B including ~$428M from the newly closed Informatica acquisition. On the cost side, Salesforce buys frontier capability rather than building it: Anthropic's Claude is a foundational model for Agentforce 360 and the preferred model for regulated industries, served inside Salesforce's trust boundary via Amazon Bedrock — per-token terms undisclosed.
ai_strategy_md: Wrap AI around proprietary customer data rather than compete on models: acquire the data-integration layer (Informatica, $8B), partner for models (Anthropic for regulated industries, plus OpenAI and Google options), price agents on consumption to escape per-seat cannibalization, and pitch 'humans + agents' to defend the seat base that AI-native rivals attack. Management markets its own deployment ('Agentforce on Help') as proof, claiming billions of agent interactions.
risk_notes_md: Agentforce's $1.2B ARR is ~3% of revenue — the AI line is growing fast but the core grows single-digits, and the stock has de-rated on fears that agents cannibalize seats faster than they add consumption revenue (shares were down roughly a third over the year to mid-2026 despite the AI milestones). Adoption breadth is contested: reported paying-customer adoption of Agentforce remains a single-digit percentage of the base. Model dependency (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) puts the scarce input on others' balance sheets; per-token economics are undisclosed.

events.title: Anthropic partnership: Claude becomes preferred model for regulated industries in Agentforce 360
events.why_it_matters: A marquee model-access edge with undisclosed dollar terms: Claude runs inside Salesforce's virtual private cloud via Amazon Bedrock, testing whether 'trust boundary' distribution is worth a premium; deepens the Salesforce-Anthropic-AWS triangle.

events.title: Q1 FY2027: Agentforce ARR crosses $1B (to $1.2B); Informatica contributes first full quarter
events.why_it_matters: The clearest datapoint yet that an incumbent SaaS vendor can build a billion-dollar AI product line — while the market debates whether it offsets seat-model erosion.
